Hacknet has probably become one of my favorite PC games to date. It's the most immersive experience I have had with a video game to date.  In short: buy it. It's worth it full price, but if you're skeptical, buy it on a sale (it goes for like 2$ on sale)

Score: 10/10 (Perfect)

Story: (10/10)

The story is told in a very interesting way. Everything (except *that* part) is text based. You read through emails, check IRC logs and text files. I won't spoil you, since even if it's not the focus of the game, the devs clearly put a lot of effort to make it as complete as possible. It's really fun to find the little hints of continuity in some random's person computer or see a chat log full of dumb inside jokes. But the story is really well made and because the game revolves on hacking

(SPOILERS FOR ENDING) [spoiler]The ending is purposefully left open-ended, but it feels conclusive and satisfying. The thrill and suspense really pays off in an incredible way. It's easily the most climactic and, in my opinion, best part of the game.[/spoiler]

Music: (10/10)

Hacknet's OST is amazing, especially if you include Labyrinths (the game's DLC) in it. It oozes charm, and it goes super well with whatever you're doing. It makes you feel epic, almost as if you were actually hacking a PC. It makes for some great background tracks, and the more "active" ones (Roller Mobster + Panic Track) create tension that complete the gameplay perfectly. In short, this OST is amazing, give it a listen even if you don't want to play the game. 

Gameplay (11/10) (I'll explain)

Hacknet's gameplay is really simple but man is it addictive. It's divised in 2 distinct phases:

1 - Researching. Look out for IP addresses, check files, read mails, accept quests, fuck around and find out, etc. This is probably the thing you'll do the most, and it's really fun to look around

2 - HACKING. This is the best part. The game has quite a lot of systems for hacking (obviously) but in short, you have 3 panels opened at all time: The Terminal, where you write your commands to do the hacking, The Display, which shows what you're doing; Checking files, looking at a web page, probing the system, etc. However, the last panel is the most important: The Ram. Basically, in Hacknet, to Hack the Net, you have to run programs, such as FTPBounce, SSLTrojan, Notes or Themechanger (the most important one). But those programs can't just run themselves forever, you have to manage your ram. You have a limited amount of storage, as you can see in the Ram section. If your program can't fit, it won't run. So you have to kill programs, wait until they're finished. This is all fun and games until you encounter a Tracker. Now, you have a time limit.

GOGOGO I NEED TO FINISH THE SSH
OH GOD WHY IS FTP TAKING SO LONG 
SHIT I HAVE TO CLEAR MY LOGS

this is the average Hacknet session
And it's one hell of a drug
The thrill of nearly failing a mission because you were sloppy with your input, forgot to clear your logs or whatever challenge you'll face, it's incredible
But to play this game, you need to type fast. Real fast. So you have to learn shortcuts and tricks to better type. This made me a better typer. It made me learn to use TAB to finish my texts faster, it made me use my Linux terminal better, and no other game can achieve that. 

Hacknet is a perfect game. Play it if you haven't.

Too naive for those are familiar with *nix. It's recommend to do the hack in real world to introduce people to *nix world. https://overthewire.org/wargames/ may be a better choice.

Let's talk about the process introduced in the game. How to scan the port? With nmap. And then? Nothing, just these four letters. What about the IP and port scan ranges? Too rough, the command should be accurate. No brain is involved. OK, now, we found the open ports, but all of them are locked, so how to hack in? Download an program from somewhere, and execute it. What?!!! How could you do that? It's so ridicules! Do you know who is that? How could you trust him without any thinking ? What if it is virus?  This is the reason that stop me from playing it anymore. Continuing talking about the hacking process, how to break the ssh port? Just type SSHhacker.exe like that of nmap. It is Sooooo boring.

Besides, the variety of commands is so poor. First, there are too few commands, you do not have find or something else. Second, the implement of existing commands are so rough: You cannot "rm *IP". You could only do "rm *" or delete one by one. For "cat" command, you could only "cat" the files under current directory, but cannot do that with directory prefix.

The reasons for not recommending are summarized below:

1. You cannot learn how to use the commands, and you may fill very uncomfortable with those naive commands.
2. You cannot learn the real hack. The name of the game is "HACKET", so what is hack? The "SSHhacker.exe" is. How to create the "SSHhacker.exe" is the key point.
3. You cannot learn safety consciousness, as said before.

This was an incredible experience. I am currently in college for IT related Network Administration and Security, and a lot of stuff in this game is related to what i'm learning. The commands you use on your terminal for example are real commands that are used in UNIX based systems.

The story was pretty engaging too, and it felt great to be able to piece things together, especially towards the end of the game where you learn a lot more about Hacknet (your OS) and why it can do things that no other hacker in-game can do. 

There were also parts that felt very intense and stressful in a great way, like near the beginning of the game is a part where you get attacked by another hacker and have to act quickly to defend yourself, or get tasked to break into a seemingly simple server only to get instantly traced and need to change your IP quickly. 

I can strongly recommend this game to anyone who wants to get a taste of the hacker/Cybersecurity world, even if it is kinda basic. And if you wanna go even further after experiencing this, there are sites like Hack The Box and TryHackMe that you can use to learn more advanced techniques and test your skills.

Having just completed the main campaign at the time of writing - with an expansion DLC and community-made storylines to go grab whenever I fancy - I find myself applauding a demonstrable, confident and competent passion project.

Sitting at a fake operating system staring at flickering text and pondering what move to try next has no right to be this satisfying, yet Hacknet remains - with very few exceptions - a title that rewards ingenuity, curiosity and player agency. People say this is one of the definitive hacking simulators, and if this is indeed the case, it's not just the fact that you can screw around so intensively in a simulated internet ecosystem that you actually break the plot - it's because you're doing what hackers actually do most of the time, which is sit back, let out a big puffy-cheek sigh of mild exasperation and mutter "ugh, how do we get around THAT one?!" or "oh wow, I probably shouldn't have been able to do this yet am being rewarded for doing so."

The game teaches a few handy command line basics for those not in the know, but it's not going to give you much of anything in the way of dangerous IRL skills, largely because the premise of the game is that a fellow hacker has created a catch-all exploit that can open any computer like a can of sardines with the right complementary toolkit. Obtaining these tools, deepening your dive into the rabbithole and exploring a series of both serious and darkly comical scenarios is very much the crux of the game, and it's enjoyable and often tense in ways simply sitting at a computer has no right to be.

At the time of this review I have 10 hours in, and that's the core campaign done and dusted - enjoyable throughout and very rarely apt to let any pacing issues slip. Missions are unlocked by communicating with shady friends (and sometimes frenemies) who closely guard IP addresses and web tools that can expand your arsenal and uncover the truth behind those lurking in the darkest reaches of the web, trashing our rights man, TRAAAASHING.

Coupled with a banging soundtrack and just enough thrills and spills to make you sit up and pay attention when you get too cocky, Hacknet couples both careful thread-pulling at mysteries and intrigue with heartpounding oh-god-oh-dear-god panic moments where the screen goes weird and you know you're up a creek you were never invited to with a paddle your trembling fingers now can't spell the name of, just as you need it the most.

Excited to try community and DLC plotlines next!
